faqs.question: What is a good short Halloween poem for a card?
faqs.answer: A two-line couplet fits any card and reads in about 4 seconds, for example: "Ten little bats hang upside down / and watch the lanterns light the town." For a sibling or best friend, a four-line verse addressed to them feels more personal.

faqs.question: How many lines should a Halloween poem for a toddler have?
faqs.answer: Two to four lines is plenty for ages 1 to 3. Pick one with a sound word they can shout, like boo, hoo or tap, and read it slowly about 3 times in a row.

faqs.question: Can I print these Halloween poems on a classroom display or something I sell?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every one of the 19 poems on this page is original and you may copy them without credit. Older poems by other writers are a different matter: in the US, only works published in 1930 or earlier are public domain as of 1 January 2026.

faqs.question: Who wrote the poem about a jack-o'-lantern with terrible teeth?
faqs.answer: Carl Sandburg, in "Theme in Yellow", printed in Chicago Poems by Henry Holt in 1916. A pumpkin narrates it and admits at the end that the children know it is only fooling, which makes it a gentle pick for young kids.

faqs.question: Does a Halloween haiku have to be 5-7-5 syllables?
faqs.answer: No. The Haiku Society of America's 2004 definitions say most English haiku use seventeen syllables or fewer, and that about twelve English syllables match the length of a Japanese seventeen-sound haiku. For children, three short lines with one clear picture matter more than an exact count.

faqs.question: How can my child memorise a Halloween poem for school?
faqs.answer: Sing it to a tune they already know. A 2026 study of 118 preschoolers found children who sang poems learned them faster and more fluently than those who recited them, and the advantage held after six months. Start about a week before 31 October.

faqs.question: What rhymes with Halloween?
faqs.answer: Green, queen, seen, screen, between, unseen and trampoline all rhyme with the last syllable of Halloween. A green-faced witch, a pumpkin queen or a ghost behind a screen each give a child an easy first line.

faqs.question: Are there Halloween poems that aren't scary?
faqs.answer: Most short ones are not. Couplets about a grinning pumpkin, a ghost in a bedroom sheet or a cat at the gate are cosy rather than frightening, and Sandburg's 1916 pumpkin poem ends by admitting it is only pretending.

faqs.question: How long should a Halloween poem be for a school assembly?
faqs.answer: A five-line limerick takes about 12 seconds to read aloud and gets a laugh, and an eight-line poem takes about 25 seconds. Longer than that and a young audience starts to drift.

faqs.question: Can I send a Halloween poem to someone who lives far away?
faqs.answer: Yes. Put it in the letter of a Halloween greeting page and send the link; the premium version adds a voice note of up to 60 seconds so they can hear you read it. For a relative who never opens links, a paper card is still the better choice.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Poems: 19 Short Original Rhymes for Kids and Cards

The best Halloween poems for kids are short: two to eight lines, one clear rhyme or image, and lines that fit a phone screen unbroken. That matters because 48.3% of the pages people share on SubhSandesh are opened on a phone, and each page created averages 11.1 views, so a poem that reads well on a small screen gets read more than once. Halloween falls on Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027.

Below are 19 original Halloween poems sorted by form. After them come a public-domain classic you can quote safely, a table matching form to use, a ten-minute writing method and the cases where a poem is the wrong pick.

## What makes a Halloween poem work when it is read aloud?

A Halloween poem is short verse about the night of 31 October and its cast: pumpkins, ghosts, bats, black cats and costumes. The ones children remember have a steady beat, a rhyme they can predict and a small surprise at the end.

Rhythm helps less than people assume. In a [2021 Open Research Europe study on meter and memory](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10445917), removing rhyme or changing syllable counts weakened recall for passages from Ariosto but made no significant difference for Dante. Its open peer reviewers split on it, so treat it as a hint.

Melody is the stronger lever for small children. A [2026 study of 118 preschoolers in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13355920) found that 4- and 5-year-olds who sang poems learned them faster and more fluently than children who recited them, and the advantage held six months later. The poems were Chinese, so the finding is about singing, not about these rhymes.

## 19 original Halloween poems, sorted by form

Every poem here was written for this page, and you may copy any of them without credit. Read-aloud times are our own estimates at a steady pace.

### 1. Two-line Halloween couplets (5 poems)

Two rhyming lines for ages 4 and up, about 4 seconds each. They fit cards and cupcake flags.

- A pumpkin on the garden wall  
  is wearing the widest grin of all.
- My ghost suit is a bedroom sheet,  
  with holes for eyes and room for feet.
- The black cat waits beside the gate  
  and purrs at anyone out late.
- Ten little bats hang upside down  
  and watch the lanterns light the town.
- Our witch forgot her magic spell,  
  so now she simply rings the bell.

### 2. Halloween haiku and senryu (4 poems)

Three short unrhymed lines for ages 8 and up, about 5 seconds each. The [Haiku Society of America's 2004 definitions](https://www.hsa-haiku.org/hsa-definitions-2004.html) note that most English haiku run to seventeen syllables or fewer, and that about twelve English syllables match a Japanese haiku's seventeen sounds. Funny ones about people are senryu.

- porch light on  
  a very small dinosaur  
  holds out a pillowcase
- first cold evening  
  the carved pumpkin's smile  
  begins to sag
- the bedsheet ghost  
  stops halfway down the stairs  
  to fix its glasses
- the sweet count  
  my little brother  
  counts his twice

### 3. Halloween limericks (2 poems)

Five lines rhyming AABBA for ages 7 and up, about 12 seconds each. The last line gets the laugh.

- A witch with a wobbly broom  
  did loop-the-loops round the room.  
  She crashed in the hall,  
  knocked a hat off the wall,  
  and blamed the whole thing on the gloom.
- There once was a pumpkin named Pete  
  who rolled himself into the street.  
  He bumped a parked car,  
  said, "I won't get far",  
  then sat on the kerb to rest his feet.

### 4. Halloween acrostic poems (2 poems)

The first letters spell a word, which suits ages 6 to 9 and classroom displays. Each takes about 6 seconds.

- **BOO**  
  Bats are out,  
  Owls are awake,  
  One more October treat to take.
- **CANDY**  
  Crinkly wrappers,  
  All in a heap,  
  "No more," says Mum,  
  Done with counting,  
  Yawning off to sleep.

### 5. Four-line Halloween rhymes for kids aged 3 to 7 (3 poems)

Rhyming pairs with sound words a toddler can shout, about 8 seconds each. Chant them between houses.

- Ghosts say boo and owls say hoo,  
  pumpkins glow a yellow hue.  
  Bats go flap and doors go tap,  
  then I go home to take a nap.
- I put on my cape and I put on my hat,  
  I practised my cackle, I borrowed the cat.  
  The cat wasn't keen and went back to its bed,  
  so I'm a witch with a teddy instead.
- Leaves crunch, crunch beneath my feet,  
  lanterns glowing down the street.  
  One more house and home we go,  
  sweets in the bag and cheeks aglow.

### 6. An eight-line Halloween poem to read aloud (1 poem)

Four rhyming couplets that tell a small story, for ages 5 and up. It takes about 25 seconds at bedtime.

> *The Night the Street Turned Orange*  
> When the sky turns plum and the day is done,  
> the lanterns wake up one by one.  
> There's a pirate, a pumpkin, a dragon in green,  
> the smallest unicorn ever seen.  
> We knock where the porch has a light in the hall,  
> we say thank you twice and we don't take it all.  
> Then home down the lane where the wind gives a moan,  
> and the moon walks behind us to see us home.

### 7. Short Halloween poems for a card (2 poems)

One quatrain each for a sibling, best friend or grandparent, about 8 seconds aloud. Write them inside a card.

- You hold the torch, I hold the bag,  
  you never let the evening drag.  
  Of all the ghosts I'll ever meet,  
  you're still my favourite on our street.
- The pumpkin's carved, the cat's in black,  
  I saved a toffee for when you're back.  
  I'm sending this to say, from here,  
  you're the best part of the year.

## Which classic Halloween poems are safe to quote or print?

In the United States, published works from 1930 and earlier are in the public domain as of 1 January 2026, according to [Duke Law's Center for the Study of the Public Domain](https://web.law.duke.edu/cspd/publicdomainday/2026/). Works from 1931 follow on 1 January 2027. Duke covers US law only, so check local rules in the UK, Canada, Australia or India.

The gentlest old Halloween poem for children is Carl Sandburg's "Theme in Yellow", printed in *Chicago Poems* by Henry Holt in 1916 ([first edition scanned on the Internet Archive](https://archive.org/details/chicagopoems00sanduoft), page 131). A pumpkin speaks, and the ending suits even a nervous five-year-old:

> "I am a jack-o'-lantern / With terrible teeth / And the children know / I am fooling."
>
> Carl Sandburg, "Theme in Yellow", *Chicago Poems* (1916)

Many popular children's Halloween poems are recent and still under copyright. For anything you will print or sell, use one of the 19 above or a poem from 1930 or earlier.

## Which Halloween poem form fits which use?

The table compares the forms on length, reading time and best use. Times are our estimates.

| Form | Lines | Read-aloud time (estimate) | Best use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Couplet | 2 | 4 seconds | Card, cupcake flag, phone message |
| Haiku or senryu | 3 | 5 seconds | Caption, older kids, classroom wall |
| Four-line rhyme | 4 | 8 seconds | Toddlers, trick-or-treat chant |
| Limerick | 5 | 12 seconds | Assembly, a laugh at the party |
| Eight-line poem | 8 | 25 seconds | Bedtime, story time, a long letter |

On a phone, the couplet and the four-line rhyme win. Their lines stay under about 40 characters and do not wrap.

## How to write a Halloween poem with a child in 10 minutes

Start with one object, not the whole holiday. Give the child two minutes to pick the pumpkin, the cat or the costume and list three words about it.

Then spend five minutes on a draft. Under-6s do best with a four-line rhyme built on a sound word like boo or tap, while 8-year-olds can manage a twelve-syllable haiku. Let the child choose the last word.

Use the last three minutes to sing it to a tune they already know, such as "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star". In the preschool study above, singing beat plain recitation for memorising poems, so the sung version is the one most likely to survive until 31 October.

## Sending a Halloween poem to one person

Two SubhSandesh templates take a poem as the letter. The [interactive Halloween card with photos and music](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) takes about five minutes to make. The recipient carves a pumpkin and reads your poem by flashlight, and its Kids tone has round blushing ghosts and no jump scares, which suits a grandchild.

The [premium cinematic Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) needs about ten minutes. It adds a voice note of up to 60 seconds, so you can read the poem aloud yourself, plus up to 12 photos and a reply box for one answer of up to 280 characters.

Across all SubhSandesh pages, 38.5% of creators add a password before sharing, and both Halloween pages offer one. If neither design fits, [browse all SubhSandesh templates](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) for a birthday or miss-you page that can carry the same poem.

## When a Halloween poem link is the wrong choice

A link is a one-person greeting, not a party tool. For a class of 25, a printed sheet of acrostics or a limerick on the whiteboard works better, and nobody needs a phone.

A grandparent who never opens links is better served by a couplet in a paper card. The templates' screens are English only, so a poem in another language sits inside English buttons.

Timing is the last trap. We have no Halloween usage data, but for Raksha Bandhan 2026, our nearest measured festival, 49.4% of 89 pages were built on the day itself. That is a small sample from a different festival, but the lesson holds: if a child will perform a poem on 31 October, start learning it a week ahead and leave the card for the day.

## Sources

- Hu, Liang and Du, *Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences*, July 2026 (singing and poem memory).
- Andreetta et al., *Open Research Europe*, version 2, February 2023 (meter and memory).
- Haiku Society of America definitions, 18 September 2004.
- Duke Law, "Public Domain Day 2026", January 2026.
- Carl Sandburg, *Chicago Poems*, Henry Holt, 1916.
